problem:
Find the two solutions to the equation $\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$ for ${0}^{∘}<x<{360}^{∘}.$

**In ascending order,** the solutions are $x=$ 
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$ and $x=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation to isolate $\operatorname{cot}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\sqrt{18} & =3\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{cot}⁡x & =3\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{18} \\ \operatorname{cot}⁡x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We can't find an equivalent equation involving tangent, since this would lead to us dividing by $0:$

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{1}{0}=\text{undefined}
$$

However, we can instead find an equivalent equation using the fact that $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}:$

$$
\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}=0
$$

In this case, we can find the principal solution as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =0 \\ x & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡0 \\ {x}_{1} & ={90}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since this value lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={90}^{∘}.$

To find more solutions, we add integer multiples of ${180}^{∘}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =x+{180}^{∘}={90}^{∘}+{180}^{∘}={270}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, our solutions are $x={90}^{∘}$ and $x={270}^{∘}.$
